analysis.investment_thesis: Spinaroo Commercial fails both pillars of the Magic Formula: earnings yield is roughly 3% (P/E 32.7) — far below my 12% threshold — and ROE of 0.21% implies return on capital near zero. This is a textbook "expensive and low-quality" stock to skip.
key_strengths: Promoter holding at 47.66% indicates some skin in the game
Small ₹41 Cr market cap leaves theoretical room for turnaround optionality
Diversified across aluminium, paper products, and machinery trading
key_risks: ROE of 0.21% — essentially zero return on capital, opposite of Magic Formula target
P/E of 32.7 implies earnings yield ~3%, deeply overvalued on EBIT basis
Commodity paper/aluminium products = no pricing power, low-moat business
red_flags: ROE < 1% suggests either near-zero earnings or bloated capital base
Trading at 32x earnings with no growth or quality justification
Micro-cap with limited disclosure and liquidity risk
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula ranks companies on earnings yield (EBIT/EV) and return on capital. Spinaroo fails both: a P/E of 32.7 translates to an earnings yield of roughly 3%, which would rank near the bottom decile of any investable universe — I want 12%+ minimum. ROE of 0.21% is not a typo-worthy number; it's a signal that this business is barely earning anything on shareholder capital, let alone the 20-25%+ ROIC I look for in "good businesses."

Combining "expensive" with "low quality" is the exact inverse of what the Magic Formula is designed to find. The paper and aluminium products segments are commoditized with structurally thin margins, and there's no evidence of a durable advantage. Even at a ₹41 Cr market cap, this is not a cigar-butt opportunity — you're paying a premium multiple for sub-par economics. Systematic rules say pass, and I pass.
